predecessors.name: German East Africa
predecessors.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

ledger.x: 1916 (6 May): the Force Publique takes Kigali and the Belgians move through Ruanda ('captured Kigali in Rwanda on 6 May'; the Belgians held Ruanda and Urundi by 17 June).
1916 (June): both districts are in Belgian hands.
1919 (30 May): Britain cedes Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium.
1922 (20 July): the League of Nations makes Ruanda-Urundi a Belgian mandate.
1946 (13 December): the mandate becomes a UN Trust Territory.
1962 (1 July): Ruanda-Urundi splits into two independent states.

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Belgian occupation of Ruanda (April-May 1916) and Urundi (June 1916); the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 30 May 1919 gave the districts to Belgium.

certainty.note: The frontiers with the Belgian Congo, Tanganyika and Uganda are not on any page opened; they follow the districts of the German East Africa years (the Kivu-Mfumbiro boundary is not covered).
